archetype.name: Play-In Team (two-big frontcourt)
archetype.definition: A roughly .500 team, sitting near the middle of the site's rankings, whose elite Giannis-and-Bam frontcourt carries an average roster and a leaky perimeter defense toward the 7-10 range of the East.

report.headline: Giannis and Bam carry it; the perimeter defense keeps it .500
report.take:
Miami is a team split in half. The frontcourt grades an A, built around the No. 1 power forward on the site, Giannis Antetokounmpo (BPM 7.5, a 33.9 USG % at a 62.8 TS %), next to Bam Adebayo, sixth among centers. Everyone else is ordinary or worse: the backcourt grades C and the wings C-. That shape produces a 7-6 record, a -1.1 Net Rtg that ranks 17th and a 16th-place site rank. This is a middle-of-the-pack team, and nothing in the profile says the record is a mirage. W vs Pt Diff is only +1, and the margin implies 6 wins against the 7 they have.

The offense is the better half, though it looks better in raw points than it is. They score 118.69 a game, fifth in the league, but they play at a 102 pace against a league average of 98.9, so the ORtg of 115.4 ranks only 12th. What works is the inside game the two bigs create: a 32.1 FT Rate (6th), a 12.4 TOV % (7th) and a 58.1 TS %. What doesn't work is the shooting (34.1 3P %, 19th) and the offensive glass (23.8 ORB %, 27th).

The defense is where the record leaks, and that is the most interesting part of the sheet. Opponents shoot 38.9 % from three, 29th in the league, and post a 57.0 Opp eFG %, 28th. Yet the rim is protected: 62.9 % at the rim (9th) on a 26.7 Opp Rim Rate (7th). Opposing point guards average 31.92 points a game against them and shooting guards 31.77, both near the bottom of the league. So the problem is guards and three-point shooting. Part of that is real: Davion Mitchell has a -5 On-Off, and Tim Hardaway Jr. is playing at a 38.7 TS % with a -9.1 BPM. Part of it is the noisiest number in basketball. Every Miami defense from 2021-22 through last year held opponents between 33.9 and 36.7 % from deep, and four of those five ranked in the top ten in defense.

The direction is good. After a 2-4 October they are 7-3 over the last ten and 4-1 over the last five, at +4.8 a game in that span. November itself was closer than its 5-2 suggests, though: 833 points scored to 829 allowed, which included a one-point overtime win and 20-plus-point losses at the Lakers and Golden State. The 44-win pace is a fair read of a team whose defense should improve but whose wing rotation will cap the ceiling.

strengths.title: Best-in-class power forward plus a top-six center
strengths.body: Giannis is first of 88 on the power forward tab, with a 7.5 BPM at a 33.9 USG %. Adebayo ranks sixth among centers at a 61.6 TS %. Their pairing explains the A frontcourt grade and nearly all of the team's positive value: the frontcourt group's 3.5 Win Shares are more than the backcourt and wings combined. This is talent rather than a hot streak, so it should hold as long as both stay healthy.

strengths.title: Efficient, low-mistake half-court offense
strengths.body: Miami gets to the line (32.1 FT Rate, 6th) and protects the ball (12.4 TOV %, 7th). That yields a 58.1 TS % that ranks 10th despite middling shooting from three. Pressure on the rim from the bigs drives it, so it should be stable. Klay Thompson's 48 threes at a 62.8 TS % give the floor-spacing the bigs need.

strengths.title: The paint is closed
strengths.body: Opponents take only 26.7 % of their shots at the rim (7th) and hit 62.9 % there (9th). Shots near the basket are the most repeatable part of a defense, which suggests the defensive foundation is sounder than the 22nd-ranked DRtg implies.

concerns.title: Guards and threes are torching them
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 38.9 % from three (29th), 3.7 points above the league, and point guards score 31.92 a game against Miami, 28th in the league. Some of this is shooting variance: every Miami team of the last five years held opponents to 36.7 % or lower. Some is personnel, since the guards defending the perimeter are not strong defenders. Expect partial regression toward the middle of the league rather than a full fix.

concerns.title: The wing rotation is a hole
concerns.body: The wings grade C-. Andrew Wiggins plays the most wing minutes yet posts a -16.9 On-Off and a -4.4 BPM. Behind the starters, Hardaway's 38.7 TS % makes him a liability. Unless the minutes shift, this caps how good Miami can be around its two bigs.

concerns.title: No second chances
concerns.body: A 23.8 ORB % ranks 27th even with Giannis and Adebayo on the floor. That leaves the offense dependent on first-shot efficiency on a team shooting 34.1 % from three.

trend.note: A 2-4 October gave way to 7-3 over the last ten and 4-1 over the last five, including double-digit home wins over Cleveland and Detroit. November's points were nearly even, though, so the climb is more modest than the record suggests.

weekAhead.headline: Three at home: two good defenses around a reeling Milwaukee
weekAhead.body:
All three games are in Miami, but two of them are against teams built to blunt what Miami does best. Houston (11-3, 2nd on the site, 10.5 Net Rtg) has the second-best offense in the league and allows the second-fewest points to opposing power forwards. Oklahoma City (9-5) is the league's best rim defense, with opponents shooting 56.7 % within four feet. Both games test whether Miami can win without its usual stream of free throws and paint points.

In between comes Milwaukee at 1-13, last in Net Rtg and 28th in DRtg. A Miami team that has won four of five should be a clear favorite in that one. A 2-1 week would confirm the climb, while 1-2 would leave Miami where its season numbers say it is: an even team.

keyMatchups.title: Giannis against Houston's PF wall
keyMatchups.body: Houston holds power forwards to 14.07 points a game, 5.13 below their usual output, both near the top of the league. Its 32.5 Opp 3P % (2nd) also means Miami's middling shooting won't get bailed out. Houston crashes the offensive glass (32.4 ORB %, 2nd), so Miami's defensive rebounding matters too.

keyMatchups.title: Adebayo against Milwaukee's F frontcourt
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee gives centers 9.4 more points, rebounds and assists combined than they average elsewhere, the worst in the league, and its frontcourt grades F. This is the night Adebayo should feast and Miami's offensive rebounding problem should fade.

keyMatchups.title: OKC's rim protection versus Miami's paint game
keyMatchups.body: Oklahoma City allows the lowest rim percentage in the league and holds centers 7.18 below their usual production, best in the league. If Miami can't get to the line, its 34.1 % three-point shooting has to carry the game.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents' three-point percentage starts falling toward Miami's historical norms. If it does, the recent surge is real; if Houston bombs away, the defense is the problem it looks like.

restOfSeason.body:
The pace says 44 wins with a slightly negative margin, and the underlying numbers support roughly that. The record isn't propped up by close-game luck, the offense's strengths (free throws, ball security, the two bigs) are durable, and the defense's worst number, opponents' three-point shooting, is the stat most likely to regress in Miami's favor. A defense that drifts back toward the middle of the league would push this into a 43-46 win team.

What keeps the ceiling down is the wing and guard rotation. The C and C- grades, Wiggins' On-Off and Hardaway's efficiency don't regress on their own. They need a change in minutes, and Larsson, day-to-day with a 65.5 TS %, is one of the few efficient options. Expect a team that fights Atlanta for the division and lands somewhere in the play-in range, with a lower-seed playoff spot the realistic upside.
swingFactors: Wing minutes moving away from Wiggins and Hardaway

confidence.note: Only 13 games, and opponent 3P % is noisy, but the profile matches recent history.
